about: Shared cases for the Markdown renderers: the app renders with Rust and the browser fallback renders with JavaScript, and both must turn each markdown into the html given here. Both tests delete every newline that comes directly before "<" or directly after ">" in the result before comparing, so the html is written without them. The cases avoid what the two renderers do differently on purpose: headings, links, block quotes, quote marks in prose, backslash escapes outside math, indented code, tilde fences and trailing spaces.

vectors.name: inline math in prose, TeX trimmed
vectors.html: The volatility is \sigma per year.

vectors.name: TeX with angle brackets, ampersand, quotes and a prime is escaped, the prime kept
vectors.markdown: Take \( a < b & c "q" f'(x) \) here.
vectors.html: Take a < b & c "q" f'(x) here.

vectors.name: underscores and stars inside math are not Markdown
vectors.markdown: Take \( a_1 * b_2 * c \) and *stress* it.
vectors.html: Take a_1 * b_2 * c and stress it.

vectors.name: bracket display math alone in its paragraph, over several lines
dollar display math alone in its paragraph, over several lines
vectors.html: a &= b \\ c &= d

vectors.name: display math inside running text stays a span
dollar display math after a line of text stays in the paragraph
inline math alone in a paragraph keeps its paragraph
a single dollar is money, never math
an unclosed double dollar is shown as written
an unclosed opener at the end, as in a cut stream, is shown as written
a stray closer is shown as written
a pair split by a blank line is not math
empty delimiters are shown as written
a code span keeps its delimiters and math after it on the same line is typeset
a fenced block keeps its delimiters
an unclosed fence, as in a cut stream, keeps its delimiters to the end
math in a list item
number columns get the num class on header and cells, a pipe inside math stays in its cell
a column that mixes numbers and words gets no class
